declarations.name: word_boundary_identity
declarations.doc: Finite ordered integration by parts, with the full terminal source boundary retained.

declarations.name: tendsto_reciprocalLogBoundary
declarations.doc: The boundary product in integration by parts vanishes at infinity.

declarations.name: tendsto_endpoint_boundary_at_anchor
declarations.doc: The actual integration-by-parts boundary product tends to zero at the stationary anchor.

declarations.name: suzukiNeumannBoundaryFlux_eq_clock
declarations.doc: The endpoint flux in the integration-by-parts law is exactly one boundary clock.

declarations.name: integral_Ioi_mul_halfLineSteinScore_with_boundary
declarations.doc: Half-line integration by parts turns the symmetric first-order score into an exact Stein covariance with its Robin/contact anomaly retained as the endpoint current `c`.

declarations.name: routeETerminalPrimeMain_eq_boundary_sub_deriv
declarations.doc: Integration by parts reassembles the identity contribution into the continuous prime main term. This is exact on the same half-open terminal interval used by the finite prime frame.

declarations.name: exists_uniform_integral_abs_deriv_suzukiBoundaryCutoff
declarations.doc: Uniform total variation of Suzuki's product cutoff. This is the quantitative input which prevents the integration-by-parts constant from blowing up as the boundary width shrinks.

declarations.name: integral_Ioi_secondDerivative_mul_eq_boundary_add
declarations.doc: Double integration by parts on a positive half-line, with all four endpoint values retained. This abstract form is used for translated theta potentials: it prevents a seam term from being silently lost when a reflected Haar packet is moved back to the positive source half-line.

declarations.name: thetaCuspShellPhaseTransform_eq_gammaBoundary_add_ward
declarations.doc: Ward integration by parts gives a second exact recurrence for the same positive shell branch. Unlike the Gamma recurrence, its remainder is visibly the phase transform of a positive density.

declarations.name: integral_id_mul_thetaCuspTiltedWardDensity_mul_sin_fifthOrderBoundary_identity
declarations.doc: Fifth-order boundary identity for the first sine moment. Compared with the fourth-order identity, one additional integration by parts exposes the second positive ground boundary term `4 f'''(0)` and retains a signed cosine remainder.

declarations.name: quasiRieszCoupling_integration_by_parts
declarations.doc: Equation (10), second form.** For `ℓ ≠ 0` and `α > 0`, `D_ℓ^{(α)} = -(α/(π ℓ)) ∫_0^π sin(ℓ k) k^{α-1} dk`.

declarations.name: intervalIntegral_byParts_of_vanishing
declarations.doc: Integration by parts with vanishing boundary values.** This is the step that iterates: after one integration by parts the integrand carries `w'`, which vanishes at both ends of any interval containing its support, so every further step is boundary-term free.

declarations.name: suzuki_spatial_integration_by_parts
declarations.doc: The exact spatial integration-by-parts step used in Suzuki (2012), equation (407). Kernel cusps `n/x` and Fredholm-solution cusps `n/a` are treated as two independent countable exceptional sets. Both weighted derivative products are proved interval-integrable across those cusps.

declarations.name: continuousPolar_stieltjesIntegrationByParts
declarations.doc: Continuous polar Stieltjes integration by parts.

declarations.name: criticalMellinStieltjesPairing_integrationByParts
declarations.doc: Stieltjes integration by parts for the complete signed critical Mellin carrier.

exploration.name: integral_hermiteRungDefect
exploration.doc: The defect is a square up to a boundary term.** One integration by parts, using only the oscillator equation.

exploration.name: norm_antiderivative_le
exploration.doc: The boundary terms of the integration by parts are controlled by the amplitude divided by the frequency lower bound.

exploration.name: quadratic_boundary_avoid_of_disjoint_boundary_ray
exploration.doc: Ray-disjoint form of boundary avoidance. After parametrizing the boundary image, it is enough for `A` to miss the explicit ray `c - t² v²`.
